questions.question: What is a sample and what does a sample rate of 16000 mean?
questions.answer: A sample is one number measuring the air pressure at an instant. 16000 means 16,000 measurements every second.
questions.hint: Think of taking a photo of the wave many times a second.

questions.question: Why is a sample rate of 16 kHz enough for recognising spoken words?
questions.answer: Speech has most of its useful information below 8 kHz and a sample rate must be about twice the highest frequency, so 16 kHz captures it.
questions.hint: Rate needs to be about double the top pitch.

questions.question: What are the three signal wires of an I2S microphone and what does each do?
questions.answer: BCLK (bit clock) times each bit, WS (word select) marks the start of each sample (and which channel it is), and SD/DATA carries the sample bits from the mic.

questions.question: The level printed is always 0. Name two wiring checks.
questions.answer: Check VDD is on 3.3 V and GND is common, and that SCK, WS and SD go to the pins named in the code; also check the L/R pin is tied to GND (not floating).
questions.hint: Power first, then the three signal wires.

questions.question: You wired the INMP441's VDD to the 5 V rail. Why is this a mistake?
questions.answer: The microphone runs at up to about 3.6 V; 5 V can damage it. Use the ESP32's 3.3 V output.
questions.hint: Remember the ESP32 runs at 3.3 V.

questions.question: Why do we average squares of samples (RMS) rather than average the samples directly?
questions.answer: Sound swings positive and negative, so a plain average is about zero. Squaring makes every value positive, so the average reflects how big the swings are.
questions.hint: What does the sum of a wave around zero come to?

questions.question: Your quiet room reads about 200 and a clap reads about 9000. Where would you put the threshold and why?
questions.answer: Somewhere in the gap, such as 3000: well above room noise so it does not trigger by itself, well below a clap so it always triggers.

questions.question: A clap triggers the hand, and the sound lasts 200 ms. Without a cooldown, what happens?
questions.answer: The level stays above the threshold for several readings and the action fires many times; a cooldown ignores triggers for a short time after the first.
